---
title: Tangled
description: "Use Tangled, a forge built on atproto: issues, pulls, comments, live events and webhooks."
icon: i-custom-tangled
---

The Tangled provider works with [Tangled](https://tangled.org), a forge built on atproto. It can read and write issues, pulls and comments, it streams live events from Jetstream and it verifies incoming push webhooks. Tangled has no reviews, checks, releases or repository contents API, so those capabilities are `false`.

## Authentication

Reading is public and needs no credentials. Writing requires an atproto session, which you get from an app password or from an OAuth client:

```ts
import { tangled } from 'forges/tangled'

const reader = tangled({}).create()

const writer = tangled({
  auth: {
    type: 'app_password',
    identifier: 'alice.example.com',
    password: process.env.TANGLED_APP_PASSWORD!,
  },
}).create()
```

With `app_password`, the provider creates a session on the PDS (personal data server) of the account. It looks for the PDS in this order:

1. The `pds` option, if you pass it.
2. The DID document, if `identifier` is a DID.
3. `https://bsky.social`.

With `oauth`, you pass the `did`, the `pds` and a `fetch` from an atproto OAuth client that signs requests:

```ts
tangled({
  auth: {
    type: 'oauth',
    did: session.did,
    pds: session.pds,
    fetch: session.fetch,
  },
})
```

## Instance and services

The `baseUrl` defaults to `https://tangled.org`. The provider uses it for web links and as the instance.

Tangled records are stored on many servers, so the provider has to read from several services. You can change each one of them with an option:

| Option | Reads | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `plcUrl` | DID documents, to find the PDS of each author | `https://plc.directory` |
| `backlinksUrl` | Records that point at a thread, such as comments | `https://constellation.microcosm.blue` |
| `handleResolverUrl` | The DID for a handle, when the `owner` of a ref is a handle | `https://public.api.bsky.app` |
| `recordsUrl` | Records, through a Slingshot-compatible cache | The PDS of each author |
| `jetstreamUrl` | The live event stream | A public Bluesky Jetstream instance |
| `apiUrl` | `request()` and `listSource: 'index'` | `https://api.tangled.org` |

## Refs and numbers

Issues and pulls are atproto records, and they are identified by their AT-URI. In a `ThreadRef`, the AT-URI is both the `number` and the `externalId`. The `owner` of a repo is the DID of its owner, and `RepoRef.externalId` is the DID of the repo.

In the refs that the provider returns, the `name` of a repo is the key of its repo record. For newer repos, that key differs from the name that people see, which `Repo.displayName` holds. You can also pass a ref that has a handle as `owner` and the visible name as `name`, which is what `parseUrl()` returns for a URL such as `https://tangled.org/@acme.example.com/widgets`. The provider resolves the handle and finds the record by its name, so the ref that it returns can differ from the one you passed.

The numbers that you see in the Tangled UI and in webhooks come from the appview, because the records themselves don't store them. The provider reports them as `displayNumber`.

A ref from a webhook has no `number` until it is matched to a record. To fill in `number` during `webhooks.ingest()`, pass a `resolveDisplayNumber(repo, kind, displayNumber)` function that returns the AT-URI.

## Thread state

The state of a thread is the latest state record that was written by the author of the thread, the owner of the repo or a collaborator. The provider ignores state records from other accounts. If another account calls `close()` or `reopen()`, the call throws `InsufficientScopeError` and writes no record.

## Listing threads

By default, `threads.list()` reads every record and works out the state of each thread, which takes several requests per thread. If you set `listSource: 'index'`, it lists from the index at `apiUrl` instead. The index takes one request per page, but its states can lag behind the records, so every listing from the index has an `index_possibly_stale` warning.

## Notifications

Notifications use the `org.tangled.temp.notification.*` lexicons. These lexicons are in Tangled's temporary namespace and can change. To enable notifications, pass `auth` and set `notificationsUrl` to the base URL of the notification service. The notification capabilities are `'experimental'` then.

Stars and follows have no thread. They appear with `kind: 'other'`, and `typeRaw` contains the type of the notification.

## Merging

Pulls are merged by the knot that hosts the repository, and there is no review step. For this reason, `merge()` and `approveAndMerge()` aren't available.

## Live events

`sources.subscribe()` streams events from Jetstream, and each item has a `cursor`. To resume a stream later, save the cursor and pass it back:

```ts
for await (const { event, cursor } of reader.sources.subscribe({
  cursor: saved,
  signal,
})) {
  console.log(event.kind, event.summary)
  saved = cursor
}
```

To close the connection, abort the signal or break out of the loop. If the connection drops, the iterator throws `SubscriptionClosedError` with the last cursor. The provider doesn't reconnect by itself, so call `subscribe()` again with that cursor.

## Webhooks

To verify deliveries, set `webhookSecret` to the secret that you configured on the hook:

```ts
const forge = tangled({
  webhookSecret: process.env.TANGLED_WEBHOOK_SECRET,
}).create()

const events = await forge.webhooks.ingest({
  headers: request.headers,
  body: await request.text(),
})
```

With each delivery, Tangled sends these headers:

| Header | Content |
| --- | --- |
| `X-Tangled-Signature-256` | `sha256=` followed by the hex HMAC-SHA256 of the body |
| `X-Tangled-Event` | The event name |
| `X-Tangled-Delivery` | The delivery ID |

A `push` delivery becomes a `push` or `ref` event. Tangled has no API to register hooks, so the management methods of `webhooks` aren't available.
